newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees return to Andean Community in August.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees return to Andean Community in August.

text.p: Trade and Industry Minister Gustavo Caillaux said Peru would make its official return to the Andean Community trade bloc in early August.
"There remain four meetings before we can sign, on the first of August or the first days of that month, the points we have agreed on," Caillaux told reporters late Thursday.
The Andean Community, which also includes Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela, announced last week in Quito Peru's full return to the group after an agreement in principle on tariff policies.
That would represent a complete volte-face since Peru's announcement in April that it was pulling out of the group definitively.

Having partially withdrawn from the group in 1992, government officials said in April Peru was making its decision final due to different views on tariff policies and allegedly unfair export subsidies by its former partners.

But a series of meetings between Peru and its partners brought agreement last week on the tariff issues, meaning the bloc can now concentrate on its negotiations with South America's other trade group Mercosur.
